name: Gaius, the wellbeloved
charge: Walking in the truth; doing faithfully to the brethren and to strangers; bringing them forward on their journey after a godly sort
summary: John wrote his third epistle to the wellbeloved Gaius, whom he loved in the truth, and rejoiced greatly when the brethren came and testified of the truth that was in him, because he walked in the truth (3 John 1:1-4). He did faithfully whatever he did to the brethren and to strangers, who bore witness of his charity before the congregation, and John told him he would do well to bring them forward on their journey after a godly sort (3 John 1:5-6).
offenseFull: A whole doctrine turns on how John words the greeting. He does not merely say the truth was in the man; he says he loved him in the truth, then says the brethren testified of the truth that was in him, even as he walked in the truth (3 John 1:1,3-4). A man is in the truth because he walks in it, and the truth is in him because he learned it from somewhere and from somebody. The teaching raises this against a doctrine going around that a man only needs the truth to be in him and does not need to be in the body: that is the subtle way of telling people they do not need a congregation and do not need the elders who taught them, and the very verse they lean on answers them. John also prayed that he would prosper and be in health even as his soul prospered (3 John 1:2), which puts the state of the soul first and makes the rest follow it.

What he actually did is set down without decoration. He did faithfully whatever he did to the brethren and to strangers, and they bore witness of his charity before the whole congregation (3 John 1:5-6). Those men had gone out for the Name’s sake, taking nothing of the Gentiles, so we ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth (3 John 1:7-8). Bringing them forward on their journey after a godly sort means paying the road, feeding them, and sending them on able to keep working. This is the plain law of the body: given to hospitality, distributing to the necessity of the saints (Romans 12:13), continuing in brotherly love and not forgetful to entertain strangers (Hebrews 13:1-2). Christ himself set the price on it: he that receives you receives me, and he that receives me receives him that sent me, and even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward (Matthew 10:40-42).
judgmentFull: John’s word over him is beloved, and the charge attached is the standard he is to keep: follow not that which is evil, but that which is good, because he that does good is of God, and he that does evil has not seen God (3 John 1:11). In the same short letter Demetrius is given a good report of all men and of the truth itself (3 John 1:12), so the commendation is not flattery, it is testimony the congregation could verify. The setting matters. John, the apostle who walked with Christ, is writing as a father to a household, the way Paul called Timothy his own son in the faith and Titus his own son after the common faith, and told the Corinthians that though they had ten thousand instructors they had not many fathers, for he had begotten them through the gospel (1 Timothy 1:2; Titus 1:4; 1 Corinthians 4:15). Gaius is not praised for rank; there is no office named for him. He kept the brethren moving, paid their way forward, and had the whole congregation testify to it. The reward Christ named for that work is the one that is never lost.

taught.title: Matthew 10: The Twelve Sent to the Lost Sheep

text.text: The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth.
Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.
For I rejoiced greatly, when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth.
I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers;
Which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well:
Because that for his name’s sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles.
We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth.
Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality.
Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward.
And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.
Demetrius hath good report of all men, and of the truth itself: yea, and we also bear record; and ye know that our record is true.
Unto Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.
For though ye have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel.
